database_summary: Small chemistry-style schema modeling molecules composed of atoms and bonds. Four tables: molecule (one row per molecule, descriptive attributes), atom (one row per atom, links to molecule), bond (one row per bond, links to molecule), connected (associative/bridge table connecting two atom rows via a bond). Data appears mostly descriptive/current-state (no explicit timestamps). Low-cardinality enums on molecule.label and bond.bond_type. Joins between atom, bond and connected are necessary to reconstruct molecular graphs; caution: connected is directional/pairwise and may duplicate rows if both directions are stored.

accepted.name: atoms_with_molecule
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  atom.atom_id AS atom_id,
  atom.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  atom.element AS element,
  molecule.label AS label
FROM atom
LEFT JOIN molecule ON atom.molecule_id = molecule.molecule_id
accepted.description: One row per atom augmented with its parent molecule attributes. Useful when you need atom-level lists with molecule-level context (filter atoms by molecule label, aggregate atoms per molecule while retaining atom details, or join to connections/bonds). | Use for: List atoms with their molecule labels; Filter atoms by molecule.label or atom.element; Join atom details to connected/bond information

accepted.name: bonds_with_molecule
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  bond.bond_id AS bond_id,
  bond.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  bond.bond_type AS bond_type,
  molecule.label AS label
FROM bond
LEFT JOIN molecule ON bond.molecule_id = molecule.molecule_id
accepted.description: One row per bond augmented with its parent molecule attributes. Useful for bond-level analyses that require molecule context (counts per molecule, bond_type breakdowns, or joining to the connected table to get endpoints). | Use for: Count bonds by bond_type per molecule; List bonds with molecule labels; Join bonds to connected endpoints

accepted.name: connections_with_atoms_and_bonds
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  connected.atom_id AS atom_id,
  connected.atom_id2 AS atom_id2,
  connected.bond_id AS bond_id,
  a1.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  a1.element AS element,
  a2.element AS element2,
  bond.bond_type AS bond_type
FROM connected
LEFT JOIN atom AS a1 ON connected.atom_id = a1.atom_id
LEFT JOIN atom AS a2 ON connected.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id
LEFT JOIN bond ON connected.bond_id = bond.bond_id
accepted.description: One row per connection (atom pair) with attributes from the bond and both endpoint atoms. Useful to reconstruct bond endpoints with element types and bond_type for graph analysis, substructure queries, or generating adjacency lists. Note: if connected stores both directions, queries using this CTE may include both orders of the same bond. | Use for: Show bond endpoints with element types and bond_type; Build adjacency lists for molecules; Find connections where elements match a pattern (e.g., element=cl)

accepted.name: atoms_per_molecule
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  atom.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  COUNT(1) AS atom_count
FROM atom
GROUP BY atom.molecule_id
accepted.description: One row per molecule with the count of atoms. Useful for ranking molecules by size, filtering molecules by atom count ranges, or joining with molecule attributes for summaries. | Use for: Which molecules have the most atoms?; Filter molecules with atom_count above/below a threshold; Combine atom_count with bond counts for density measures

accepted.name: bonds_per_molecule_by_type
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  bond.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  bond.bond_type AS bond_type,
  COUNT(1) AS bond_type_count
FROM bond
GROUP BY bond.molecule_id, bond.bond_type
accepted.description: One row per molecule and bond_type with the count of bonds of that type. Useful to analyze bond_type distributions within molecules or to compute bond-type ratios when joined to total bond counts. | Use for: Distribution of bond types per molecule; Identify molecules with particular bond_type compositions; Compute fraction of double/triple bonds per molecule

accepted.name: molecule_atom_bond_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  m.label AS label,
  COALESCE(a.atom_count, 0) AS atom_count,
  COALESCE(b.bond_count, 0) AS bond_count
FROM molecule AS m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(1) AS atom_count FROM atom GROUP BY molecule_id
) AS a ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(1) AS bond_count FROM bond GROUP BY molecule_id
) AS b ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id
accepted.description: One row per molecule providing counts of atoms and bonds. Useful for quick molecule-level summaries combining atom and bond counts for comparisons or as inputs to ranking or selection logic. | Use for: Compare molecules by atom_count and bond_count; Find molecules with atoms > bonds or vice versa; Use atom/bond counts to filter molecules for downstream analysis

accepted.name: molecule_adjacency_list
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  connected.atom_id AS source_atom_id,
  connected.atom_id2 AS target_atom_id,
  connected.bond_id AS bond_id,
  bond.bond_type AS bond_type
FROM connected
LEFT JOIN atom AS a ON connected.atom_id = a.atom_id
LEFT JOIN bond ON connected.bond_id = bond.bond_id
accepted.description: One row per molecule-atom endpoint pair expressing adjacency as a compact edge list: molecule_id, source atom, target atom, bond_id and bond_type. Useful to feed graph algorithms or to export molecule connectivity. This preserves the connection grain for each recorded connection. | Use for: Produce adjacency lists for graph traversal per molecule; Export edges with bond types for visualization; Detect isolated atoms by checking absence in this adjacency list

accepted.name: atom_degree_per_molecule
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.atom_id AS atom_id,
  a.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  COUNT(1) AS degree
FROM connected AS c
LEFT JOIN atom AS a ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id
GROUP BY c.atom_id
accepted.description: One row per atom computing its degree (number of connected edges recorded in connected). Useful to find terminal atoms (degree=1), highly connected atoms, or to summarize degree distributions per molecule. | Use for: Find atoms with degree = 1 (endpoints); Aggregate average degree per molecule; Identify hubs within molecules

accepted.name: molecule_rank_by_atom_count
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.molecule_id AS molecule_id,
  m.label AS label,
  COALESCE(a.atom_count, 0) AS atom_count,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(a.atom_count, 0) DESC) AS atom_count_rank
FROM molecule AS m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(1) AS atom_count FROM atom GROUP BY molecule_id
) AS a ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id
accepted.description: One row per molecule with its atom_count and a dense rank by atom_count (1 = largest). Useful to select top-N molecules by size or to assign size buckets. This CTE uses atoms_per_molecule semantics but produces a windowed rank column. | Use for: Return top-N molecules by atom_count (apply WHERE on atom_count_rank externally); Compare rank positions across molecules; Bucket molecules into quantiles by atom_count
